slides.label: Cover
slides.title: 10 **Neuroscience-Backed** Brain Hacks to Train Your ==Supercomputer Brain==
slides.hook: 90% of people forget what they learn within **24 hours**. Not because they're not smart — because they're using the __wrong methods.__

slides.label: Why This Matters
slides.method: Why Most People Never Learn Fast
slides.heading: Your Brain is a **Supercomputer** Running the Wrong Software
paragraphs: The average person spends **thousands of hours** studying, reading, and watching content — yet retains almost nothing after 7 days. It's not an intelligence problem. It's a __method problem.__

Neuroscience has now identified the exact biological mechanisms — **neuroplasticity, synaptic strengthening, and dopamine-driven encoding** — that determine how fast and how deeply information actually sticks.
Master these mechanisms and you don't just learn faster. You ==think differently.== You retain more. You perform at a level most people believe is reserved for geniuses.
slides.blockquote: The brain is not a vessel to be filled, but a fire to be kindled.

steps.title: Study for 25 focused minutes
steps.desc: One topic, zero distractions. Phone off. Single tab open. Full attention on the material.

steps.title: Close everything completely
steps.desc: Shut the book. Pause the video. Create a total blank slate — no peeking allowed.

steps.title: Write everything you remember
steps.desc: Brain dump every concept onto paper. This forces retrieval — not passive recognition.

steps.title: Return and check your gaps
steps.desc: Compare your notes to the source material. Only your gaps need to be re-studied.

steps.title: Repeat at 24h · 3 days · 7 days
steps.desc: Spaced intervals permanently lock the material into your long-term memory storage.

steps.title: Eliminate All Distractions

steps.title: Mandatory Break + Recall

bullets.title: Chunk Your Information
bullets.desc: Break all content into 3–5 item groups. Your working memory holds only ~7 items at once.

bullets.title: One Screen, One Task Only
bullets.desc: Multitasking reduces IQ by 10 points temporarily. Single-tasking always outperforms.

bullets.title: Pre-Study Brain Dump
bullets.desc: Write every distracting thought before starting. This clears valuable working memory bandwidth.

bullets.title: Build Mental Models First
bullets.desc: Link new information to existing frameworks. This reduces cognitive load by up to 60%.

bullets.title: Use Dual-Channel Encoding
bullets.desc: Pair images with words. Dual channel theory shows they are processed in parallel for deeper encoding.

slides.label: Hack 08 — Sleep is Memory
slides.method: Sleep Neuroscience — Matthew Walker Ph.D. · UC Berkeley
slides.heading: Sleep is Not Rest. Sleep is **Memory Installation.**
slides.quote: During deep sleep, your hippocampus replays everything you learned that day — transferring it to the neocortex for permanent storage. Skip sleep and you delete the file.
slides.attr: Matthew Walker, Ph.D. · Why We Sleep (2017)

cards.title: Set Micro-Goals
cards.desc: Define tiny wins every 25 minutes. Each completion releases a dopamine spike that fuels the next session.

cards.title: Exercise Before Study
cards.desc: Just 20 minutes of cardio before studying raises BDNF levels by 200% — literally growing new brain cells.

cards.title: Cold Exposure
cards.desc: A cold shower post-study spikes dopamine by 250% above baseline and keeps it elevated for 3–5 hours.

cards.title: Celebrate Your Effort
cards.desc: Reward the process, not just the result. This conditions your brain to crave the learning state itself.

cards.title: Morning Sunlight
cards.desc: 10 minutes of sunlight within 30 minutes of waking sets your circadian rhythm for peak focus by 10 AM.

cards.title: No Phone in the Morning
cards.desc: Checking your phone first thing blunts your dopamine sensitivity for the entire rest of the day.

slides.method: Scott Young's UltraLearning Framework · MIT Challenge
slides.heading: 5 More **Power Moves** for Your Brain

cards.title: The Feynman Technique
cards.desc: Explain any concept to a 10-year-old. Gaps in your explanation reveal exact gaps in your understanding.

cards.title: Interleaving Practice
cards.desc: Deliberately mix different topics during a study session. Harder but produces 43% better long-term transfer.

cards.title: Desirable Difficulty
cards.desc: Always study at the edge of your current ability. Material that feels easy builds zero new neural pathways.

cards.title: Elaborative Interrogation
cards.desc: Ask 'Why is this true?' for every single fact you study. Forces deep semantic processing and long retention.

cards.title: Diffuse Mode Thinking
cards.desc: Walk, shower, or simply relax. Your default mode network solves complex problems passively while you rest.
